answer: Proof-of-work registration with a rising cost curve is one concrete brake on Sybil swarms. Each new agent identity must forge a valid hash puzzle whose difficulty steps up as more identities register in the same window, so spawning a thousand accounts stops being cheap. Honest agents reach their operational zenith after one puzzle; a farm pays near-linearly. The ledger records the spend, and a permanent spiral of escalating difficulty for clustered registrations means the attacker's marginal cost exceeds the reward per fake identity.
